cards.title: Recovery hardness for sparse planted dense subgraphs
cards.formal: Assuming the planted-clique hypothesis below, is exact recovery of the planted vertex set impossible in randomized polynomial time throughout the interior of the blue region in the source’s Figure 2? Fix \(0<\alpha<1\), \(c>1\), and \(\max\{\alpha,\frac12+\frac{\alpha}{4}\}<\beta<\frac12+\frac{\alpha}{2}\). With \(p_N=cq_N=\Theta(N^{-\alpha})\) and mean planted size \(K_N=\Theta(N^\beta)\), the proposed obstruction rules out algorithms whose probability of recovering the entire planted set tends to one. This card selects exact recovery and strict interior exponents; critical boundary lines and weaker overlap guarantees are separate targets.
cards.why: Separates recognizing the presence of a hidden community from locating all of its vertices. The sparse gap remains a useful test of how computational limits depend on the inference task, even after related reduction and restricted-algorithm results.
cards.status_note: Read the original model, Hypothesis 1, Figure 2 discussion and fixed-size caveat; checked the COLT 2023 conjectures and Corollary 11 and both COLT/arXiv 2026 models and low-degree theorems. Searches through 12 September 2026 found no resolution of the selected interior under the ordinary planted-clique premise. Exact recovery in the binomial model and strict interior exponents are explicit scope choices from the broader caption.

progress.text: The source proves planted-clique-based hardness in the smaller red region and leaves recovery hardness in the blue region open.
COLT 2023 establishes a detection–recovery gap under secret-leakage planted clique for a different, dense background regime.
COLT 2026 gives results for general planted subgraphs, including low-degree lower bounds, without settling this unrestricted sparse target.

cards.definitions:
The graph has labeled vertices [N]={1,…,N}. Include each vertex independently in a hidden set S with probability K_N/N. Conditional on S, draw each unordered edge independently with probability p_N if both endpoints are in S, and q_N otherwise. There are no loops. Thus |S| is binomial with mean K_N, not fixed to K_N. The algorithm sees the entire graph and knows N,K_N,p_N,q_N, but receives no planted vertices or location information. K_N may be taken as a supplied integer; the realized |S| remains hidden.

Exact recovery means outputting a subset Ŝ⊆[N] with Pr[Ŝ=S]→1. Probability averages over S, graph edges and internal algorithmic randomness. Output size is unrestricted because |S| is random. Running time is N^{O(1)} on every input and random tape, with constants allowed to depend on the fixed regime. Parameters have explicit rational encodings of polynomial bit length; the constant-ratio version uses a fixed rational c>1. This is the ordinary finite-input interpretation of the phase diagram.

The Θ notation requires upper and lower positive constant multiples of the stated powers for all sufficiently large N; those constants do not grow with N. Probabilities satisfy 0<q_N<p_N<1. The target concerns every fixed interior exponent pair and its admissible parameter sequences, without demanding uniformity as exponents approach a boundary with N.

The premise is Hypothesis 1 of the source for every fixed γ∈(0,1/2]. In planted-clique detection, the null is G(n,γ). The alternative draws G(n,γ), chooses a uniform k_n-vertex subset, and fills in all missing edges within it. Whenever limsup log(k_n)/log(n)<1/2, every randomized polynomial-time test has liminf of its type-I plus type-II error at least one. No partition or other clue to the clique's location is supplied. This is an average-case detection assumption, not worst-case clique NP-hardness.

Detection merely decides whether planting occurred. A densest-K-subgraph approximation returns a K-vertex set with many edges, which need not be S. Partial or almost-exact recovery permits support mistakes and requires a separate overlap criterion. The fixed-size planting model chooses S uniformly among sets of exactly K_N vertices; Section 4.2 and Appendix B distinguish it from the binomial model. Concentration of |S| around its mean alone does not transfer arbitrary algorithms between them.

The original blue region is max{α,1/2+α/4}≤β≤1/2+α/2. The formal question deliberately keeps its strict interior, avoiding equality cases whose hidden constants and logarithmic factors are not fixed by the caption. It is not asserted equivalent to every boundary or approximate-recovery variant.
cards.answer_criterion: Establish the conditional obstruction to probability-1−o(1) exact recovery in this independent-vertex planting model throughout the strict interior, or give a polynomial-time exact-recovery algorithm in some such regime with its guarantees proved. Restricted low-degree, spectral or MCMC lower bounds do not establish the all-algorithm claim. Results needing planted-clique side information or a different density or planted-size model must retain those qualifications.

context_blocks.title: Detection and recovery have different thresholds
context_blocks.text: In the source’s sparse regime, efficient detection is available above β=1/2+α/4, while its cited efficient exact-recovery algorithms require β>1/2+α/2. The blue region lies below the latter and above the earlier hardness or statistical limits.

context_blocks.title: The caption covers more than one possible output task
context_blocks.text: Figure 2 names recovery, while adjacent text also asks about constant-factor densest-K-subgraph approximation. This card retains recovery and explicitly chooses exact support success in the original binomial planting model.

context_blocks.title: Later reduction-based gaps have different scope
context_blocks.text: Bresler and Jiang obtain a gap using a stronger planted-clique premise with a known partition and one planted vertex in each part. Corollary 11 uses a dense background and a shrinking probability difference, not the sparse constant-ratio regime here. Their exponent notation therefore cannot be inserted directly into the 2015 diagram.

context_blocks.title: The 2026 lower bound restricts the algorithm class
context_blocks.text: Huleihel treats general planted structures, with main results for dense probabilities. Theorem 7 rules out sufficiently low-degree polynomial estimators. It is not a lower bound for all randomized polynomial-time recovery algorithms in this sparse model.

cards.context:
In the source’s sparse regime, efficient detection is available above β=1/2+α/4, while its cited efficient exact-recovery algorithms require β>1/2+α/2. The blue region lies below the latter and above the earlier hardness or statistical limits.

Figure 2 names recovery, while adjacent text also asks about constant-factor densest-K-subgraph approximation. This card retains recovery and explicitly chooses exact support success in the original binomial planting model.

Bresler and Jiang obtain a gap using a stronger planted-clique premise with a known partition and one planted vertex in each part. Corollary 11 uses a dense background and a shrinking probability difference, not the sparse constant-ratio regime here. Their exponent notation therefore cannot be inserted directly into the 2015 diagram.

Huleihel treats general planted structures, with main results for dense probabilities. Theorem 7 rules out sufficiently low-degree polynomial estimators. It is not a lower bound for all randomized polynomial-time recovery algorithms in this sparse model.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
